analyst.summary: Adani Total Gas keeps growing volumes at a healthy mid-teens pace and is expanding its CNG/PNG network at the fastest clip in its history, but its profit is not growing with it: FY26 consolidated profit rose only about 0.2% for the full year despite 16-18% revenue growth, because a government cutback in subsidised (APM) gas allocated to the CNG segment is forcing the company onto costlier open-market gas, and rising debt is adding to interest costs. Despite that earnings stagnation, the stock trades near 110-120 times trailing earnings, roughly 4-6x the sector's average multiple and a ~380% premium to comparably-profitable peer Gujarat Gas. Q1 FY27 results land within the next 1-2 days (board meets 21-Jul, call 22-Jul-2026) and will be the key near-term read-through on whether the APM/margin pressure is easing or worsening. Separately, the Adani promoter group's US legal overhang (DOJ bribery case, SEC settlement) appears to be resolving favourably through 2026, which is a group-level tailwind but not an ATGL operating-fundamentals argument. No quant score exists yet for this name.
